blocks.text: It should also be noted that the שפנים sephanim of the Jews, that is, χοιρογρυλλίους [choirogryllious], or ἀρκτομῦας [arktomyas] if you prefer, have certain features in common with the rabbits of Spain: namely the eyes, the head and the tip of the tail, as Teixeira observes. Moreover, [col. 1017] their hind feet are longer than their fore feet, they move by leaping, and they likewise ruminate, although they have teeth in both jaws, and they dig themselves underground hiding places in which they lie hidden by day. Therefore, as the Jews do today, so the Carthaginians seem once to have given the Hebrew name שפן saphan to rabbits; and hence it is that Spain was called שפניה, Σπάνια [Spania], that is, cuniculosa [full of rabbits], as Celtiberia is in Catullus, which we have already pointed out above ^{c)}. Let others, however, be the judges of this.
